content.thinking:
I'm drafting a postmortem and starting with the symptom: account pages failed for many shoppers, stated without a number. Next I'm laying out the causal chain, beginning with the failed account page requests.

I'm working through the causal chain for the postmortem now. The errors began at 12:21 with a ZeroDivisionError in the spend-summary code, and I'm checking which change switched that path on. The monthly-spend flag was turned on by an admin, and a later unrelated change can be ruled out because the errors started before it landed.

I'm settling on the root cause now: the monthly-spend flag routes account pages into a spend calculation that divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month. I'm checking that the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 is that division, though the line alone doesn't show why the count is zero.

I'm deciding how to word the root cause without a line number: the boundary turns the ZeroDivisionError into a failed page, and the spend-summary module is where the failure lives. Next I'm noting a first contributing factor, that the flag went on for all traffic at 12:21 with no staged rollout.

I'm noting that the contributing factor is the missing check: nothing I've seen exercised the flag-on path against shoppers with no purchases this month before the flag went live in production. I'm also thinking the action item should be to require flag-on tests for gated paths before enabling them.

I'm noting that the third contributing factor is that nobody was paged, and I'm weighing whether that belongs in the list at all, since alerting held as configured before the incident. I'm leaning toward recording it as a finding with an action item to link the alert to on-call paging, because a person being told sooner would have shortened the response.

I'm weighing whether to note that nobody was paged as a contributing factor or a finding, and I'm leaning toward listing it under what went wrong, with a process action item to link the alert to on-call paging.

I'm setting up the follow-up items now: a pre-enable check that runs the tests with each feature flag on before it can be switched on in production, and a gradual rollout that starts with a small share of traffic and widens only while the error rate holds. I'm also noting that the alert isn't linked to on-call paging, so it should be.

I'm finishing the root-cause wording now: the fix doesn't change the outcome for shoppers who never bought anything, so switching the flag back on before the fix lands would likely fail account pages again for those shoppers. I'm also stating the root cause in plain terms, a setting that sent account pages through new monthly-spending code, which likely fails for shoppers who bought before but not this month. Next I'm noting that Argus read the flag provider's history further back than the investigation's earlier reads.

I'm noting that Argus read the flag provider's history beyond where the investigation's reads ended and found the later unrelated-feature change. I'm also recording that the investigator settled on one candidate tying the error to the flag change, that the mitigation agent reverted the flag and then confirmed the service recovered, and that the code-fix agent proposed a draft fix. Last, nobody was paged, and the investigation's change reads stopped short of where they needed to go.

I'm settling the last points of the postmortem: the go-well and go-wrong items, and whether the unpaged alert belongs among the findings. The next part is about the assumptions, which I'm still working through.

I'm checking whether a deploy could explain the onset, and the read found none in the day before. I'm also ruling out the second flag change, since it was turned on after the errors began at 12:21 and turning only the monthly-spend flag off brought the service back with it still on.

I'm working out the Step 1 wording: shoppers' account page requests failed, with no figures given. For Step 2 I'm noting that the ZeroDivisionError came from the spend-summary code from the onset minute, which the logs don't show before then.

I'm writing the step-by-step causal chain for the postmortem, tying the account page errors to the monthly-spend flag switched on in production. Next I'm noting that the flag sent account pages into a calculation that a shopper with no purchases this month would trigger.

I'm adding a note that the auto-revert of the flag on an error alert would be a separate action from the staged rollout, and I'm leaving it out of the list for now.

action_items.item: Before a feature flag can be switched on in production, require the service's tests to pass with that flag on.
Add test fixtures for shoppers with purchase history but no purchases in the current month, and run them on every flag-gated account page path.
Switch feature flags on for a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the error rate stays at its baseline.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Before the onset, the logs read show failures only from shoppers closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: The feature flag an-unrelated-feature, which admin switched on at {P2.1}. The errors had already begun at the onset, before this change. Switching only monthly-spend-feature off brought the service back while an-unrelated-feature stayed on.
A deploy. The read of production changes returned no deploys, only the flag change.

causal_chain.step: That code started running on account page requests when admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. From that minute, the flag's evaluations went from all off to all on.
With the flag on, account pages reached a monthly spend-per-item calculation that fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a setting that sent account pages through new monthly-spending code, and that code likely breaks for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The failing division would have shown up before the flag reached shoppers, and the switch would not have been made.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for all of the service's evaluations at once. No staged rollout was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing code before the error rise showed, so fewer account pages would have failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate, C1, which tied the failures to the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the ZeroDivisionError log line.
Argus read the flag provider's history beyond where the investigation's change reads ended, and found the later an-unrelated-feature change.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back to OFF, an action that can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the revert from the service's own metrics before Argus marked the incident mitigated.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/581, for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's spend by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the call raises ZeroDivisionError. The error boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py then turns it into a failed account page.
input.still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
